🇲🇽🎒 <u>PROFECO DEPLOYS 55 BACK-TO-SCHOOL FAIRS NATIONWIDE</u>

Mexico's consumer protection agency Profeco is rolling out 55 back-to-school fairs across the country starting July 31, running through September 4: school uniforms, books, backpacks, stationery and shoes at preferential prices, plus free haircuts, medical certificates and birth certificate services. Mexico City's main fair lands at Expo Reforma on August 15-16. Defending the family budget is public policy, not charity.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>VULCAN LOSES AT ICSID: MEXICO PAYS LESS THAN 1%</u>

US firm Vulcan Materials sued Mexico at ICSID for over $1.7 billion after its Calica quarry in Quintana Roo was shut down over environmental violations. The tribunal threw out nearly every claim: Mexico will pay about $17 million — less than 1% of the demand — tied to a single closure in January 2018, under Peña Nieto. Sheinbaum was clear: the company must now repair the environmental damage in Playa del Carmen, and the land stays a Natural Protected Area. The investor-state arbitration racket blinked.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>AMERICAN SOCIETY OF MEXICO DENIES ANTI-SHEINBAUM PLOT</u>

After Contralínea exposed the June 6 dinner where the American Society of Mexico hosted opposition figures pushing the "narcogovernment" line against President Sheinbaum, its president Larry Rubin exercised his right of reply: AmSoc is "not a political party nor an actor of the opposition," just a neutral binational forum since 1942. His own defense gives the game away: "as hosts we cannot be responsible for the guests who decide not to attend" — the government was invited, the destabilizers showed up. The denial confirms the nerve was touched.

💰🇲🇽 <u>CARTEL MONEY GOES TO SCHOOL — IN FLORIDA</u>

Wendy Amaral Arévalo, ex-partner of Abigael "El Cuini" González Valencia, financial boss of Los Cuinis and the CJNG, pleaded guilty in a US court to violating Kingpin Act sanctions: she paid over half a million dollars in tuition contracts at Florida's elite IMG Academy sports school with drug money. She faces up to 10 years in prison and a $10 million fine; sentencing is set for October 2. Washington sanctions the money, but the money lives — and spends — in the United States.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>TRUMP: "I DON'T CARE" ABOUT THE USMCA</u>

Trump told Fox News he doesn't care about renewing the trade deal with Mexico and Canada: "I really don't want to do it. I'd rather be independent. Mexico and Canada need us; we don't need them." Days earlier, Washington killed the 16-year extension both partners wanted and imposed annual reviews through 2036. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard's reply: Mexico is the United States' biggest customer. And while Trump claims his tariffs are pulling automakers out of Mexico, Kia just put $649 million on the table for Nuevo León.
